item: A Stop inside a gazetteer Wikidata request is the switch's, not that batch's refusal: it no longer counts as refused, feeds the give-up streak, or ends as gave-up (R353)
summary: fetch_wikidata named only the refusals the guarded path raises before a request (NetworkBlocked, TransportUnavailable); a Stop landing inside the request arrives as the raw transport error, so the cut batch was counted refused and fed refused_in_a_row. The next loop turn reads the switch, but on the last batch there is none (the run ended without an airplane note and a refused count, the R337 shape), and when the cut batch was the third consecutive refusal the run ended as gave_up_after_refusals for a server that never refused. The failed request now reads the switch (R320, never a wider regex): the batch is not_asked, stopped_by_airplane_mode is true, nothing is added to refused or to the streak. No new key. Cause confirmed by reading the loop, then by the red-before run: two of three tests fail on the old code (last batch; third consecutive refusal); the control (an ordinary transport failure with the switch clear is still refused and still gives up) passes on both.
